title: What would you do to find the most popular game?
description: A question from the book asks what to do with the favourite-games list to find the most popular game. The video builds a table of games and counts, using the grouping and counting of the solved example.
teaching_notes: One idea: a table keeps the count of each answer together so the largest count can be seen. The book also asks for other ways, so grouping names into boxes is mentioned.

source: Figure it Out: what would you do to find the most popular game
video_script.why: The child chooses a table as a tidy home for the counts of each game.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own list of the favourite games of 31 children
video_script.anchor: the favourite-games list of Ziva and Laksh
video_script.payoff_line: Arrange the data in a table, count the children for each game, and pick the largest count.

final_answer.value: Arrange the data in a table and count the children for each game
final_answer.spoken: arrange the data in a table and count the children for each game

names.Ziva: girl who makes the favourite-games list with Naresh
names.Laksh: boy who collects favourite games with Navya

hold_back: arrange the data in a table
never_show: the final counts of the games
maths_rules: Six games, so the table has six rows.
The counts in the second column must add up to 31.
video_script.design: A blank two-column table beside the list: games on the left, counts on the right.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the favourite games of a class.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>What would you do to find the most popular game?

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the list of thirty one children and their favourite games.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: table with a column for Game and a column for Number of children; the six game names fill the first column

narration: <bookmark mark='names'/>Step one, write each game once in the first column of a table.

marks.count: the counts fill the second column, one for each game
marks.check: the counts are added and match the number of children in the list

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step two, count the children for each game and write each count in the second column.
<bookmark mark='check'/>The six counts should add up to thirty one, so no child is missed.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: look down the second column for the largest count

marks.look: an arrow runs down the second column and stops at the largest count

narration: <bookmark mark='look'/>Step three, look down the second column for the largest count.
The game beside it is the most popular game.

beats.on_screen: Answer: arrange the data in a table, count the children for each game, and pick the largest count; grouping names into boxes is another way

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Arrange the data in a table, count the children for each game, and pick the largest count.
<bookmark mark='other'/>Grouping the names into boxes, one for each game, is another way.
